You are a programming expert. 
You will be provided with a patch used to fix a bug. 

Your task is summarize the modifications made in the patch.
Your summary should consist of two parts, modifications in each file and their relationships.

From 4942dc6638b07b5326b6d2faa142635c559e7cd5 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Andrew Murray <andrew.murray@arm.com>
Date: Fri, 17 Jan 2020 13:43:24 +0000
Subject: [PATCH] KVM: arm64: Write arch.mdcr_el2 changes since last vcpu_load
 on VHE

On VHE systems arch.mdcr_el2 is written to mdcr_el2 at vcpu_load time to
set options for self-hosted debug and the performance monitors
extension.

Unfortunately the value of arch.mdcr_el2 is not calculated until
kvm_arm_setup_debug() in the run loop after the vcpu has been loaded.
This means that the initial brief iterations of the run loop use a zero
value of mdcr_el2 - until the vcpu is preempted. This also results in a
delay between changes to vcpu->guest_debug taking effect.

Fix this by writing to mdcr_el2 in kvm_arm_setup_debug() on VHE systems
when a change to arch.mdcr_el2 has been detected.

Fixes: d5a21bcc2995 ("KVM: arm64: Move common VHE/non-VHE trap config in separate functions")
Cc: <stable@vger.kernel.org> # 4.17.x-
Suggested-by: James Morse <james.morse@arm.com>
Acked-by: Will Deacon <will@kernel.org>
Reviewed-by: Marc Zyngier <maz@kernel.org>
Signed-off-by: Andrew Murray <andrew.murray@arm.com>
Signed-off-by: Catalin Marinas <catalin.marinas@arm.com>

diff --git a/arch/arm64/kvm/debug.c b/arch/arm64/kvm/debug.c
index 43487f035385..7a7e425616b5 100644
--- a/arch/arm64/kvm/debug.c
+++ b/arch/arm64/kvm/debug.c
@@ -101,7 +101,7 @@ void kvm_arm_reset_debug_ptr(struct kvm_vcpu *vcpu)
 void kvm_arm_setup_debug(struct kvm_vcpu *vcpu)
 {
 	bool trap_debug = !(vcpu->arch.flags & KVM_ARM64_DEBUG_DIRTY);
-	unsigned long mdscr;
+	unsigned long mdscr, orig_mdcr_el2 = vcpu->arch.mdcr_el2;
 
 	trace_kvm_arm_setup_debug(vcpu, vcpu->guest_debug);
 
@@ -197,6 +197,10 @@ void kvm_arm_setup_debug(struct kvm_vcpu *vcpu)
 	if (vcpu_read_sys_reg(vcpu, MDSCR_EL1) & (DBG_MDSCR_KDE | DBG_MDSCR_MDE))
 		vcpu->arch.flags |= KVM_ARM64_DEBUG_DIRTY;
 
+	/* Write mdcr_el2 changes since vcpu_load on VHE systems */
+	if (has_vhe() && orig_mdcr_el2 != vcpu->arch.mdcr_el2)
+		write_sysreg(vcpu->arch.mdcr_el2, mdcr_el2);
+
 	trace_kvm_arm_set_dreg32("MDCR_EL2", vcpu->arch.mdcr_el2);
 	trace_kvm_arm_set_dreg32("MDSCR_EL1", vcpu_read_sys_reg(vcpu, MDSCR_EL1));
 }
-- 
2.25.1

### Modifications in Each File

1. **File: `arch/arm64/kvm/debug.c`**
   - A new variable `orig_mdcr_el2` is introduced to store the original value of `vcpu->arch.mdcr_el2` at the beginning of the `kvm_arm_setup_debug` function.
   - A conditional check is added to compare `orig_mdcr_el2` with the current value of `vcpu->arch.mdcr_el2`. If they differ and the system has VHE (Virtualization Host Extensions), the new value of `mdcr_el2` is written to the system register using `write_sysreg`.

### Relationships Between Modifications

The modifications in `arch/arm64/kvm/debug.c` address a bug related to the timing of writing the `mdcr_el2` register on VHE systems. Previously, the value of `mdcr_el2` was not updated until after the vCPU was loaded, leading to incorrect behavior during the initial iterations of the run loop. The new code ensures that any changes to `arch.mdcr_el2` are immediately reflected in the `mdcr_el2` register when the debug setup is performed, thus eliminating the delay in applying changes to `vcpu->guest_debug` and ensuring that the correct configuration is used right from the start of the run loop.

Root cause:<Root cause>

The code statements that lead to the bug are:
```c
vcpu->arch.mdcr_el2 = __this_cpu_read(mdcr_el2) & MDCR_EL2_HPMN_MASK;
```
```c
vcpu->arch.mdcr_el2 |= (MDCR_EL2_TPM | MDCR_EL2_TPMS | MDCR_EL2_TPMCR | MDCR_EL2_TDRA | MDCR_EL2_TDOSA);
```
```c
if (has_vhe() && orig_mdcr_el2 != vcpu->arch.mdcr_el2)
```
Reason:
The bug occurs because the value of `arch.mdcr_el2` is set to a calculated value only after the vCPU has been loaded, leading to the initial iterations of the run loop using a zero value for `mdcr_el2`. This results in incorrect behavior and delays in applying changes to `vcpu->guest_debug`.

The code statements that fix the bug are:
```c
unsigned long mdscr, orig_mdcr_el2 = vcpu->arch.mdcr_el2;
```
```c
if (has_vhe() && orig_mdcr_el2 != vcpu->arch.mdcr_el2)
    write_sysreg(vcpu->arch.mdcr_el2, mdcr_el2);
```
Reason:
The fix involves storing the original value of `mdcr_el2` before it is modified and then writing the updated value to `mdcr_el2` immediately if changes are detected. This ensures that the correct value is used during the initial iterations of the run loop, preventing the use of a zero value and ensuring that changes to `vcpu->guest_debug` take effect without delay.
